Changelog

0.26

  • RUSSOLO, a fourth engine: noise, logic and broken buffers, re-making the techniques of Robert Heel's Noisferatu. Seventeen kinds — HOLD, DUST, GATES, CRACKLE (noise); NOR, XOR, RING, CASCADE, CLANG (oscillators combined bit by bit); CHUNKS, JUMP, WANDER, BEND, QUAD (generated buffers read with their addresses bent); BLIPS, WALK, CHORD (chance-driven tones) — at a third of the sample rate in 10 bits, crushed and sample-held further as each sound says. A key gates it and sets its pitch; one organism a layer, as CALIGULA. Its macros: the kind's two parameters, CRUSH and CHAOS. The paths lean it: AMBIENT to chords, dust, crackle, blips and walks, clean and slow; EXPERIMENTAL to logic and bent buffers, crushed and abrupt. Presets: 64 for it too.
  • Sessions are a fuller snapshot: they now also keep each layer's granulator character and its latched notes (which sound again on load). The master reverb was already kept. Sessions and presets saved before load as they were.

0.25

  • Voices from a shared pool: twelve voices for all the layers instead of two fixed per layer. A layer takes as many as its notes need — a twelve-note chord on one layer, single notes on others. With all twelve busy, a new note takes the oldest release (any layer), else its own layer's oldest held note, else the oldest held anywhere.

0.24

  • Sessions are written to and read from the flash a sector at a time: about 50 KB of RAM freed (more than half of it), for more voices and a fourth engine to come. Nothing changes in use; every session saved before loads.
  • The start-up screen's name fits the screen.

0.23

  • Overdubs in and out: hold PLAY and the chosen layer's loops appear on the white keys (the first loop on the leftmost, then each overdub), lit while they play and shown on the screen. A key takes its loop out or brings it back in — while they play, at once and from its start; while stopped, choosing what PLAY will start. PLAY pressed and let go still starts and stops the loops. Sessions keep which loops are out.

0.22

  • Macros: the black key before SHIFT turns EDIT on (lit) and off. While it is on, KNOB 1–4 are four macros that reshape the chosen layer's sound live, chosen for each engine and kind of sound — FM: BRIGHT, DETUNE or SKEW, GRIT, MOTION; ANIMA: TONE, GRAINS / AIR / FM / VOWEL / DRIVE, SPACE, MOTION; CALIGULA: EDGE, DEPTH, CHAOS or ECHO, HAND or PULSE. The middle is the sound as drawn. Sessions and presets keep them; HOME starts a new sound in the middle.
  • FM in tune: a slip in the FM generator put nearly every operator ratio near an even multiple, so patches played about two octaves above the key and lost most of their designed ratios (bells, near-harmonic beating). New sounds now have the ratios they were designed with, at the key's pitch. Sounds saved before (sessions, presets) come back exactly as they were.

0.21

  • Presets: SHIFT + SAVE opens the chosen layer's engine's presets, 64 an engine (P1–P64), four a page. SAVE held saves the layer's sound into the slot chosen (asking OVERWRITE? over a full one), SAVE loads it.
  • Richer, smarter generators (generation 1):
    • FM: eight new families — CHOIR, BOWED, HOLLOW, BLOOM, TIDE, SHARDS, STATIC, WIND; every patch shaped with care (no screaming sidebands, brightness scaled down the keyboard), gentler mutations, and several patches drawn and measured, keeping one whose brightness suits the path.
    • ANIMA: six new kinds — TIDE, CHOIR, SHARDS, BOWL, DUST, MACHINE; the filter follows the keyboard; the second oscillator's interval suits the path; AMBIENT sounds get a space to ring in.
    • CALIGULA: four new species — LITANY, UNDERTOW, WIRE, MOTH; four new tunings (fourths, a minor seventh, open fifths, a quarter-tone cluster); the hand plays phrases, often on a pulse; a bed that the gates never close.
  • Sounds saved before (in sessions) come back exactly as they were: the older generators are kept as they were, and a test checks it.

0.20 — Tonitor

  • The firmware is now called Tonitor (it was developed as ACOUSMA). The FM-1 shows the new name at start-up and over USB ("FM-1 Tonitor"); sessions saved before keep working.
  • A browser installer: install from Chrome, Edge or Opera over Web MIDI, no tools needed.
  • The website, the logo, the manual online.

0.19

  • SHIFT + PLAY with no loop playing starts every loop there is, all together from their starts.

0.18

  • On the SESSIONS page, SAVE held saves into the slot shown: an empty one asks SAVE NEW, a full one asks OVERWRITE? (on NO until turned to YES).
  • Slots holding a session show their number in red; empty slots in grey with EMPTY.

0.17

  • ANIMA EXPERIMENTAL made much wilder and more textured: crushed rates, folding, dragged noise, scattered grains, fast tremolo, a ringing comb.
  • SHIFT + PLAY stops every loop on every layer, from any layer.
  • The level meter runs across the bottom of the screen, above the pan; the level is shown in %.
  • Long messages (EXPERIMENTAL) fit the screen.

0.16

  • Generative paths: AMBIENT and EXPERIMENTAL on the two leftmost black keys, per layer, for every engine.
  • CALIGULA's slow swells and long releases now play as designed.
  • Under heavy load the note just played is never the one dropped (ANIMA notes no longer go silent beside CALIGULA); SHIFT shows the audio load.

0.15

  • Latching: hold keys, then press SHIFT. On the SCALE page SELECT chooses the root, ALGORITHM the scale.

0.14

  • SHIFT (the rightmost black key) and latched keys.

0.13

  • CALIGULA played from the keys like the other engines, a simulated hand on its plates.

0.12

  • CALIGULA, a third engine.

0.1 – 0.11

  • FM and ANIMA engines; six layers with two voices each; a free looper per layer, then up to ten overdubs; layer level, pan and reverb send; the master reverb; 64 session slots; scales on the white keys; the DJ filter, the granulator and the crush per layer.

Tonitor is by Nuno Zimas, built on Felucca and SLOOP. Firmware: GPL-3.0. Website and logo: MIT. Source on GitHub.
